newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait eager to cut foreigners in workforce.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait eager to cut foreigners in workforce.

text.p: Kuwait, whose citizens form about a third of its population, plans to reduce dependence on foreigners and encourage the private sector to hire more Kuwaitis, a minister was quoted on Saturday as saying.

Planning Minister Ali al-Zmei'a said in a written response to parliament that Kuwait's population was 1.96 million at the end of 1996, including 1.25 million foreigners who reside in the oil-rich Gulf Arab state, al-Watan newspaper reported.
Kuwait planned to replace foreigners in the public sector by Kuwaitis at an annual rate of 10 percent and "increase the ability of the private sector to absorb" Kuwaitis, he said.
Zmei'a put the foreign workforce at 876,586, including 555,420 Asians, 293,651 nationals of other Arab countries, 5,688 Europeans and 3,330 Americans.
The state employs more than 90 percent of Kuwaitis in the workforce.
The government planned to make it less attractive for the private sector to hire foreigners by obliging it to provide them with health care and raising residency and entry fees, the minister said.
Kuwait might also "subsidise" the salaries of Kuwaitis in the private sector and link facilities granted to a private business with the number of Kuwaitis it employs, Zmei'a said.
Kuwaitis are attracted by high government salaries and benefits which the private sector is unwilling to match.

In an apparent reference to the controversial issue of some 100,000 stateless Arabs who reside in Kuwait and are seeking citizenship, the minister said the government did not plan to use naturalisation to increase the number of Kuwaiti nationals.
Zmei'a said Kuwait hoped to maintain a 3.4 percent annual population growth rate for Kuwaiti nationals "for the longest period possible".
